questions.q: What does a blue pill mean in Tableau, and what does it produce in the view?
options: A continuous field — it produces a measurable axis
A field that can't be used in a chart
A field with an error in it
A discrete field — it produces distinct, separately-labeled headers
questions.explain: Blue means discrete — the field produces separate headers, one per distinct value, rather than a continuous axis.

questions.q: What does a green pill mean, and what does it produce?
options: A continuous field — it produces a measurable axis instead of separate headers
A field that has been filtered
A calculated field specifically
A discrete field — it produces separate headers
questions.explain: Green means continuous — the field produces a single measurable axis with even spacing, rather than a set of separate headers.

questions.q: When you first drag a date field into a Tableau view, what type does it default to?
options: Continuous (green) — always
It depends entirely on the date level you picked
Discrete (blue) — regardless of which date level (Year, Month, etc.) you've chosen
Dates cannot be discrete or continuous, only dimensions can be
questions.explain: Dates default to discrete when first added to a view. Date level (Year, Month, ...) and date type (discrete vs. continuous) are two separate, independently-set properties on the same field.

questions.q: Why does a continuous date field matter specifically for building a proper time-series line chart?
options: Continuous dates remove the need for a date field entirely
A continuous date produces one connected axis, so a line chart traces a single smooth trend line rather than broken segments between separate discrete headers
Continuous dates are required before Tableau will let you use the Line mark type at all
It doesn't matter — discrete and continuous dates always produce identical line charts
questions.explain: A discrete date field creates separate headers, so a line chart built on it draws disconnected segments between them. A continuous date field creates one unbroken axis, letting the line chart draw a single connected trend.

questions.q: Are date level (Year, Quarter, Month, Week, Day) and date type (discrete vs. continuous) the same setting?
options: No, date type only applies to numeric fields, never to dates
Yes — choosing Month automatically makes the field continuous
Yes — choosing a Date Value automatically makes the field discrete
No — they are two independent settings on the same field, and can be combined in almost any way (e.g., a continuous Month or a discrete Year)
questions.explain: Date level and date type are separate, independently-configurable properties of the same date field — you can pair a discrete Month with a continuous Year, or any other combination, depending on what the chart needs to show.
